title: Publish the Anchors: A Minimal Interoperability Standard for Text Embedding Spaces, with a Cross-Vendor German Migration Study
author: Egbal Waldmann
measure: nDCG@10; 'percent of full re-embed' is nDCG@10 relative to embedding documents and queries with the new model

testbeds.MIRACL-de: German MIRACL with passage judgements, 305 queries
testbeds.Archive: a private archive of German documents, 300 generated questions; only aggregates are released

claims.statement: With an orthogonal map fitted on all in-domain anchor pairs, a translated index keeps this share of the nDCG@10 of a full re-embed.
Translating queries into the old space instead keeps this share.
Of 2,920 measured combinations, none is better than keeping the old model beyond the noise of the query sample.
A translated index inherits the limits of the model that wrote it: from a much weaker old model it stays below that model.
With 1,000 anchor pairs the orthogonal map keeps this share of a full re-embed.
An index with nine tenths of its vectors translated and the rest re-embedded is worse than a fully translated one.
Wikipedia anchors in place of anchors from the archive itself cost this many percentage points of a full re-embed on the Archive, pair by pair.
Anchors embedded in the query role change orthogonal query translation by this many points of nDCG@10 (hundredths), within or near the noise.
The rank correlation between neighbour overlap of two anchor matrices and the outcome of translation is positive within a testbed, but no measure gives the size of the loss.
On the Archive, a translated index fused with BM25 is above BM25 alone.

proposal.Embedding Space Card: what must be identical for two vectors to be comparable
proposal.anchor corpus: public passages whose embeddings every provider publishes for every model version
proposal.Adapter Manifest: ties a map between two spaces to a measured retrieval result
